    Track cluster evolution over time

    Source: R/cluster-evolution.R
    sm_cluster_evolution.Rd

    Analyses how research clusters evolve across time windows. For each pair of consecutive windows, clusters are linked either by the overlap of the terms in their titles (link_by = "terms", the default) or, after one clustering of the whole corpus, by their shared cluster_id (link_by = "cluster_id").

    Usage

    sm_cluster_evolution(
  corpus,
  time_windows = NULL,
  link_threshold = 0.3,
  link_by = c("terms", "cluster_id"),
  noise = 0L,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

    Arguments

    corpus

    An sm_corpus object with a cluster_id column in corpus$works and a year column.

    time_windows

    A list of integer vectors defining year ranges for each window, or NULL (default). If NULL, windows are created automatically by splitting the year range into roughly equal periods.

    link_threshold

    Numeric between 0 and 1; minimum Jaccard similarity to link two clusters across time windows. Defaults to 0.3. Not used with link_by = "cluster_id".

    link_by

    How clusters of consecutive windows are linked. "terms" (default) compares every pair of clusters by the Jaccard similarity of their title terms and keeps the pairs that reach link_threshold; use it when each window was clustered on its own. "cluster_id" follows a clustering of the whole corpus (for example from sm_cluster_hdbscan()): every cluster present in both windows gives one transition to itself.

    noise

    The cluster_id that marks noise, the works no cluster claims: 0L by default, as sm_cluster_hdbscan() assigns. With link_by = "cluster_id" noise gets no transition. NULL treats every id as a cluster; set it for clusterings that use another noise label or a real cluster 0. Not used with link_by = "terms".

    call

    Caller environment for error reporting.

    Value

    A list with two components and the attribute link_by (the linking mode used):

    snapshots

    A tibble with columns window, cluster_id, n_works, top_terms (a character string of representative terms) and share (the cluster's share of the window's clustered works, noise included, so the shares of a window sum to 1).

    transitions

    A tibble with columns from_window, to_window, from_cluster, to_cluster, jaccard (the Jaccard similarity of the two clusters' title terms, rounded to 4 digits; 0 when neither has any) and n_shared (the number of shared title terms).

    Details

    The function:

    1. Splits works into time windows.

    2. Within each window, identifies the cluster composition.

    3. Between consecutive windows, links clusters. A work sits in exactly one window, so clusters cannot share works; "terms" therefore compares the terms of their titles and links the pairs whose Jaccard similarity reaches link_threshold, while "cluster_id" links each cluster to itself and reports the title-term Jaccard of its two windows without filtering.

    With one clustering of the whole corpus, the same cluster_id in two windows is the continuity, and large clusters rarely reach the term threshold, so "terms" can report no transition at all. Use link_by = "cluster_id" there.

    See also

    Other clustering: sm_cluster_hdbscan(), sm_cluster_kmeans(), sm_cluster_label(), sm_cluster_leiden()

    Examples

    # \donttest{
corpus <- sm_example_corpus(with_embeddings = TRUE)
corpus <- sm_cluster_kmeans(corpus, k = 5)
#> ✔ K-means clustering complete.
#> ℹ 5 clusters, sizes range from 27 to 49.
evo <- sm_cluster_evolution(corpus)
#> ✔ Cluster evolution computed across 3 time windows.
#> ℹ 50 transitions found above threshold 0.3.
evo$snapshots
#> # A tibble: 15 × 5
#>    window    cluster_id n_works top_terms                                  share
#>    <chr>          <int>   <int> <chr>                                      <dbl>
#>  1 2015-2017          1       8 clinical; outcomes; spatial; transcriptom… 0.154
#>  2 2015-2017          2       8 expression; gene; biomarker; cross; disco… 0.154
#>  3 2015-2017          3      11 spatial; transcriptomics; biomarker; cell… 0.212
#>  4 2015-2017          4      12 spatial; transcriptomics; meta; biomarker… 0.231
#>  5 2015-2017          5      13 clinical; outcomes; drug; resistance; cro… 0.25 
#>  6 2018-2020          1      16 cell; rna; seq; single; microenvironment   0.246
#>  7 2018-2020          2       7 cell; clinical; cohort; outcomes; rna      0.108
#>  8 2018-2020          3      15 clinical; outcomes; spatial; transcriptom… 0.231
#>  9 2018-2020          4      14 cancer; colorectal; randomized; trial; ce… 0.215
#> 10 2018-2020          5      13 microenvironment; tumor; biomarker; disco… 0.2  
#> 11 2021-2024          1      15 biomarker; cell; discovery; randomized; r… 0.181
#> 12 2021-2024          2      12 cancer; checkpoint; colorectal; cross; im… 0.145
#> 13 2021-2024          3      19 spatial; transcriptomics; biomarker; case… 0.229
#> 14 2021-2024          4      14 clinical; expression; gene; outcomes; bio… 0.169
#> 15 2021-2024          5      23 cancer; colorectal; drug; resistance; cli… 0.277
evo$transitions
#> # A tibble: 50 × 6
#>    from_window to_window from_cluster to_cluster jaccard n_shared
#>    <chr>       <chr>            <int>      <int>   <dbl>    <int>
#>  1 2015-2017   2018-2020            1          1   0.871       27
#>  2 2015-2017   2018-2020            1          5   0.788       26
#>  3 2015-2017   2018-2020            1          3   0.879       29
#>  4 2015-2017   2018-2020            1          4   0.879       29
#>  5 2015-2017   2018-2020            1          2   0.742       23
#>  6 2015-2017   2018-2020            3          1   0.727       24
#>  7 2015-2017   2018-2020            3          5   0.758       25
#>  8 2015-2017   2018-2020            3          3   0.848       28
#>  9 2015-2017   2018-2020            3          4   0.848       28
#> 10 2015-2017   2018-2020            3          2   0.710       22
#> # ℹ 40 more rows

# one clustering for the whole corpus: follow each cluster id
evo <- sm_cluster_evolution(corpus, link_by = "cluster_id")
#> ✔ Cluster evolution computed across 3 time windows.
#> ℹ 10 transitions link the same cluster id in consecutive windows.
evo$transitions
#> # A tibble: 10 × 6
#>    from_window to_window from_cluster to_cluster jaccard n_shared
